name: NAAFI Bacon Roll
desc: A soft white roll, two rashers, brown sauce, wrapped in greaseproof paper and handed over by someone who has been up since four. The Airbridge runs on them. Restores 150 HP.

name: Mess Tin Stew
desc: A thick stew of beef, carrots and barley served in a tin dish and eaten standing up. It does not look like much, and it is exactly what you want after a long flight. Restores 220 HP.

name: Aircrew Boiled Sweets
desc: A paper bag of boiled sweets, passed down the cabin at take-off and landing. Sucking one helps your ears pop, and nobody has ever asked what flavour it is. Restores 70 HP.

name: Calentita
desc: Gibraltar's national dish: a baked cake of chickpea flour, olive oil, water, salt and pepper, hot from the oven in a round tin. The Genoese brought it with them, and the Rock took it for its own. Eat it with black pepper. Restores 150 HP.

name: Gibraltar Rosto
desc: Macaroni baked in a rich tomato sauce with beef or chicken, a Sunday dish on the Rock. Rosto is a Gibraltarian word for a dish nobody else seems to have a name for, and it tastes of a grandmother's kitchen. Restores 210 HP.

name: Main Street Fish and Chips
desc: Crispy battered fish and thick chips, in paper, eaten on a bench in Casemates Square while a seagull plans its next move. The vinegar has seen more sun than the fish. Restores 180 HP.

name: Siege Cannonball
desc: A cast-iron ball from the Great Siege of 1779 to 1783, found in a tunnel and still heavy enough to knock a Spanish gun-boat off course. The Garrison fired red-hot shot at the floating batteries, and it worked.

name: Halloumi
desc: A firm, squeaky Cypriot cheese of sheep's and goat's milk, folded round a little mint and grilled until it browns. It is served hot with a squeeze of lemon, and it squeaks against the teeth. Restores 170 HP.

name: Loukoumi
desc: Cypriot delight: soft rose-scented squares dusted in icing sugar, handed out with coffee in every kafeneio. It sticks to everything and tastes like a flower. Restores 90 HP.

name: Carob Syrup
desc: A thick, dark syrup boiled from carob pods, tasting a little like toffee and a little like treacle. It is the old sweetener of Cyprus, poured over bread and yoghurt, and the word 'carat' comes from the carob seed. Restores 130 HP.

name: Flamingo Feather
desc: A long, pale-pink feather found on the shore of the Akrotiri Salt Lake. Flamingos get their colour from the shrimp and algae they strain from the water, and wear it like a badge of what they ate.
effect_text: Speed up when it first comes out.
